stories.headline: OpenAI Shuts Down Sora Video App, Redirecting Compute to Robotics and Enterprise

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on March 24 it is discontinuing Sora, including the consumer app, developer API, and video features in ChatGPT
OpenAI is redirecting compute resources toward ChatGPT, a 'superapp' combining ChatGPT, Codex, and web browser, and long-term bets on autonomous robots
Disney's planned multiyear character licensing agreement—covering Mickey Mouse, Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars characters—has been cancelled
The Sora research team will continue focusing on world simulation research to advance robotics for real-world physical tasks
Applications Chief Fidji Simo directed employees to avoid 'side quests' and concentrate on agentic systems enhancing productivity
Sora launched in February 2024, reached #1 on Apple App Store in October 2025, but declined in user interest; the shutdown comes ahead of OpenAI's expected IPO

stories.headline: OpenAI Raises Additional $10B, Bringing Record Fundraise Past $120B Ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar announced the company is raising an additional $10 billion, bringing total fundraise to 'north of $120 billion'
New $10B tranche co-led by Andreessen Horowitz, D.E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG, and T. Rowe Price, with Microsoft also participating
OpenAI's February 2026 revenue matched its entire Q1 2025 revenue, and Codex—its largest agentic deployment—grew 5x since January
Friar signaled IPO readiness, stating the round 'de-risks' the path to becoming a public company
OpenAI expects to reach a 50-50 split between enterprise and consumer revenue by end of 2026

stories.headline: Arm Unveils AGI CPU, Its First Data Center Chip, Co-Developed with Meta on TSMC 3nm

key_facts.fact: Arm announced the AGI CPU on March 24, its first production data center processor, manufactured on TSMC's 3-nanometer process
Meta is the lead partner and will deploy the AGI CPU alongside its own custom chips in its data centers
Arm claims the chip delivers 2x performance per rack compared to x86 platforms from Intel and AMD
The chip targets the growing demand for CPUs in agentic AI workloads, where inference is becoming more important than training
Arm shares jumped 6.5% in extended trading; the company expects the chip to add billions in annual revenue
The move represents a strategic shift for Arm, which has historically relied only on IP licensing and royalties rather than producing its own silicon

stories.headline: Databricks Launches Lakewatch Agentic SIEM Powered by Claude, Acquires Two Startups

key_facts.fact: Databricks launched Lakewatch, an agentic SIEM using AI agents powered by Anthropic's Claude for threat detection and response at petabyte scale
Databricks acquired Antimatter (deal closed last year) and SiftD.ai (deal closed March 23) to underpin the product
SiftD.ai co-founder Steve Zhang was former chief scientist at Splunk who created the Search Processing Language
CEO Ali Ghodsi declared 'This will be the year we see AI killing the SIEM' at RSAC conference in San Francisco
Lakewatch claims up to 80% lower total cost of ownership vs traditional SIEM with no per-byte license fees
Databricks frames the product as deploying defensive AI agents to counter offensive AI agent attacks at machine speed

stories.headline: Google DeepMind and Agile Robots Partner to Deploy Gemini Robotics in Factories

key_facts.fact: Agile Robots and Google DeepMind formed a strategic research partnership to integrate Gemini Robotics foundation models into industrial robots
Agile Robots has deployed over 20,000 robotics solutions worldwide and employs more than 2,500 people
Target sectors include electronics manufacturing, automotive, data centers, and logistics
Data collected from real-world robot deployments will feed back into improving the Gemini AI models, creating a continuous improvement loop
Agile Robots has raised more than $270 million in venture capital since its 2018 founding in Munich

stories.headline: Amazon Acquires Fauna Robotics and Its $50K Sprout Humanoid for Consumer Market

key_facts.fact: Amazon acquired Fauna Robotics, whose Sprout humanoid is a $50,000, 3-foot-6-inch, 50-pound bipedal robot designed for homes and schools
Fauna was founded in 2024 by former Meta and Google engineers; its approximately 50 employees will join Amazon in New York
Disney and Hyundai's Boston Dynamics were among Sprout's early customers before the acquisition
Amazon already operates more than 1 million robots across its warehouse operations
Amazon also acquired Rivr last week for last-mile delivery automation, signaling a broader robotics acquisition push

stories.headline: Highlight AI Raises $40M Series A from Khosla Ventures for AI Agent Operating System

key_facts.fact: Highlight AI raised $40 million in Series A funding led by Khosla Ventures for its 'intelligent operating system for teams and AI agents'
Investors include 359 Capital, General Catalyst, Valor Equity, Common Metal, Makers Fund, Collaborative Fund, Arcadia, and SV Angel
Vinod Khosla stated the gap between AI capabilities and coordination systems exists 'across every industry and at every scale' and that an OS maintaining human-machine alignment 'becomes imperative'

stories.headline: Arm Unveils 136-Core AGI CPU, Its First-Ever Data Center Chip, With Meta as Lead Partner

key_facts.fact: Arm announced the AGI CPU, its first-ever production chip for sale, featuring up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores manufactured on TSMC's 3nm process.
The chip claims more than twice the performance per server rack as Intel silicon and up to $10 billion in savings per gigawatt of data center capacity.
The AGI CPU has a 300W TDP, supports DDR5-8800 with up to 6TB capacity per chip, 96x PCIe Gen 6 lanes, and CXL 3.0 memory expansion.
A reference rack design supports 30 blades with two CPUs each in a 36kW air-cooled configuration, yielding 8,160 total cores per rack.
Meta Platforms is the lead launch partner, with OpenAI, Cloudflare, Cerebras, SAP, and Lenovo also listed as initial customers.
Arm expects the new chip unit to generate $15 billion in annual sales within five years, representing a fundamental shift from IP licensing to direct silicon sales.

stories.headline: Cadence and NVIDIA Expand Partnership for AI-Driven Chip Design With Millennium M2000 Supercomputer

key_facts.fact: Cadence Design Systems and NVIDIA are expanding their collaboration to develop AI-driven engineering tools for chip and system design using agentic AI systems.
The partnership integrates agentic AI agents that can autonomously translate design inputs into workflows, generate chip designs, detect errors, and manage long engineering processes.
The Cadence Millennium M2000 supercomputer uses NVIDIA Grace CPUs and Blackwell GPUs, delivering up to 80x higher processing throughput with reduced power consumption.

stories.headline: Baker Hughes and Google Cloud Partner on AI-Enabled Power Optimization for Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Baker Hughes announced a collaboration with Google Cloud to develop AI-enabled power optimization and sustainability solutions for the global data center sector, announced at CERAWeek 2026.

The collaboration combines Baker Hughes' turbomachinery and power systems expertise with Google Cloud's AI and data analytics to optimize how power is generated, managed, and consumed in data centers.
Baker Hughes CEO Lorenzo Simonelli called data center power infrastructure 'one of the most critical drivers of global electricity needs.'

stories.headline: Amazon's Zoox Brings Purpose-Built Robotaxis to Austin and Miami, Quadruples SF Service Area

key_facts.fact: Zoox announced plans to deploy its purpose-built robotaxis (no steering wheel or pedals) in Austin, Texas and Miami, Florida later in 2026, after nearly two years of test vehicle operations in both cities.
Trips in the new cities will initially be limited to Zoox employees and their families before the Explorer program opens to the public.

Zoox's San Francisco service area is quadrupling in size to cover the eastern half of the city, while Las Vegas is doubling destinations to include The Sphere, T-Mobile Arena, and the Convention Center.
CEO Aicha Evans said Zoox is ready to start charging fares once it receives regulatory approval.

stories.headline: BRINC Unveils Guardian, World's First Starlink-Connected Drone for 911 First Response

key_facts.fact: BRINC released Guardian, described as 'the most capable 911 response drone ever' and the world's first drone with integrated Starlink satellite connectivity.
Guardian has 62-minute flight time, 8-mile range (vs 3 miles for current systems), 4K video with 640x zoom, dual HD thermal cameras, and a speaker/siren 3x louder than police vehicles.
Guardian Station, its robotic charging nest, automatically swaps batteries and redeploys to new missions without human intervention, enabling 24/7 operations.
The drone automatically loads mission-specific payloads including defibrillators, flotation devices, and Narcan depending on the emergency type.
Over 900 public safety agencies currently use BRINC products, including 20%+ of U.S. SWAT teams. Motorola Solutions holds exclusive North American reseller rights.

stories.headline: Shield AI and Swiss Destinus Complete European Drone Autonomy Test Campaign in Spain

key_facts.fact: Shield AI and Swiss startup Destinus completed a two-month autonomy integration and flight test campaign in Segovia, Spain, flying the Hornet counter-drone interceptor with Shield AI's Hivemind software.
Hivemind autonomously adapted flight paths in real-time, including rerouting away from geofenced locations that were altered while the drone was airborne.
Hivemind operates onboard the aircraft rather than via ground control, enabling operation in GNSS-denied and communications-degraded environments.
Next phases will expand to advanced mission planning, terrain-aware flight profiles, and coordinated multi-platform behaviors across multiple Destinus platform families.

stories.headline: DJI Spin-Off ZYT Readies Autonomous Driving Foundation Model, Signs Volkswagen as First Car Customer

key_facts.fact: ZYT (Zhuoyu Technology), a spin-off from drone maker DJI, will demonstrate a 'mobility foundation model' for autonomous driving at the Beijing auto show in April, with CEO Shen Shaojie saying the AI outdrives him on Shenzhen streets.

The AI was trained not just on road-driving video but on footage from drones, robots, vacuum cleaners, motorcycles, and people carrying cameras, allowing it to work across vehicle types and geographies.
ZYT partners with companies covering 98% of the Chinese truck market and will deploy highway truck driving systems with XCMG, SHACMAN, and SINOTRUK in H1 2026, with upgrades taking just six weeks.
Volkswagen has signed on as ZYT's first passenger car customer, with the first VW model using the system slated for 2027 and tests underway in Europe.
ZYT is targeting a Hong Kong IPO possibly in 2027.

stories.headline: US Space Force Reassigns GPS III Launch to SpaceX After ULA Vulcan Mid-Flight Anomaly

key_facts.fact: The US Space Force reassigned a GPS III satellite launch from ULA's Vulcan rocket to SpaceX's Falcon 9 due to an ongoing investigation into Vulcan's performance.
During a February 12, 2026 military satellite launch, the Vulcan rocket 'sparked and twisted on its axis mid-flight,' leading to a pause of all military Vulcan launches.
SpaceX is expected to launch the GPS III payload before late April, avoiding significant schedule delays. In exchange, ULA will handle the USSF-70 mission originally assigned to SpaceX.
Seven additional national security missions were originally scheduled for Vulcan, creating uncertainty about ULA's ability to fulfill its manifest.

stories.headline: Russia's Bureau 1440 Launches First 16 Operational LEO Broadband Satellites to Rival Starlink

key_facts.fact: Bureau 1440, the Russian aerospace firm developing a LEO satellite system for global broadband, launched its first batch of 16 operational satellites on Monday, March 24.
The company described the deployment as 'a transition from experiment to the creation of a communication service,' marking a shift from test to operational phase.
Russia remains far behind SpaceX's Starlink network, which has deployed over 10,000 satellites since 2019, while Russia's initiative is just beginning.

stories.headline: German Startup Isar Aerospace Attempts Second Spectrum Launch From Norway for European Orbital Sovereignty

key_facts.fact: Isar Aerospace is attempting a second orbital launch of its Spectrum rocket from Andøya Spaceport in northern Norway on March 25, after its first attempt in 2025 ended in failure.
If successful, Spectrum would mark the first time a European private company reaches orbit from continental European soil, a milestone for European space sovereignty.
The mission is ESA's qualifying second launch under its Boost! commercial space transport program, carrying five cubesats and a science experiment.

stories.headline: US Sends Iran 15-Point Ceasefire Plan via Pakistan as Trump Declares 'We've Won This'

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration sent Iran a 15-point ceasefire proposal covering sanctions relief, civilian nuclear cooperation, rollback of Iran's nuclear program, IAEA monitoring, missile limits, and Hormuz shipping access.
The plan was delivered to Iran by Pakistan, which has offered to host renewed negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
Trump told reporters 'We've won this. This war has been won' and claimed Iran had offered a 'prize' related to oil and gas, while Iran's parliament speaker denied any negotiations with the US.
An Iranian military spokesperson mocked US ceasefire attempts on Wednesday, insisting that the Americans were 'only negotiating with themselves.'
The US-Israeli war on Iran, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, is now in its fourth week after launching on February 28, 2026.

stories.headline: Israel Announces Seizure of Southern Lebanon Up to Litani River as 'Defensive Buffer'

key_facts.fact: Defense Minister Israel Katz announced Israeli forces would 'control the remaining bridges and the security zone up to the Litani,' a river 30km north of the border, amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon's territory.
Israel has destroyed five bridges over the Litani River since March 13 and accelerated demolition of homes in Lebanese border villages.

Hezbollah called the Israeli occupation an 'existential threat' to the Lebanese state. Senior lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah said: 'We have no choice but to confront this aggression and cling to the land.'
Israeli strikes have killed over 1,072 people in Lebanon including 121 children, and displaced more than one million people since the escalation began.
Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for formal annexation of southern Lebanon, declaring 'the new Israeli border must be the Litani.'

stories.headline: Russia Launches Record 948 Drones at Ukraine in 24 Hours, Signaling Spring Offensive

key_facts.fact: Russia launched nearly 1,000 strike drones (948) at Ukraine over a 24-hour period on March 24, the largest aerial attack since the war began, breaking the previous record of 728 drones.
Ukraine intercepted or disabled 906 of the drones at a 95.5% success rate.
At least six people were killed and 46 injured across Ukraine, with strikes hitting civilian areas including near the 17th century St. Andrew's Church in Lviv.
Zelenskyy said the scale of the strikes showed Putin 'has no real intention of ending this war' and called for stronger international pressure on Moscow.
Ukraine's military reported total Russian losses on March 24 included 1,220 personnel, 2,459 UAVs destroyed, and 51 artillery systems.

Ukraine retaliated with its own record attack, with Russia's Defense Ministry reporting it shot down 389 incoming Ukrainian drones in the largest overnight attack on Russian territory since the war began.

stories.headline: Pentagon Deploys 2,000 82nd Airborne Troops to Middle East, Total Reinforcements Near 7,000

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon ordered about 2,000 soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division's Immediate Response Force to deploy to the Middle East, including Maj. Gen. Brandon Tegtmeier and two battalions of ~800 soldiers each.

The 82nd Airborne is trained to parachute into hostile or contested territory to secure key positions and airfields, distinguishing this from prior Marine deployments focused on embassy support and evacuation.

Combined with 4,500+ Marines already en route, total additional ground forces dispatched since the conflict started approaches 7,000, supplementing the 50,000 troops already assigned to Operation Epic Fury.
The Senate Armed Services Committee is scheduled to receive a classified briefing from Pentagon officials on Wednesday regarding the deployment.

stories.headline: Iran Imposes $2M Transit Toll on Hormuz Shipping and Turns Back Container Vessel

key_facts.fact: Iran has begun charging transit fees of up to $2 million per voyage on commercial vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, creating an informal toll on the waterway that normally carries a fifth of the world's oil and gas.

The IRGC Navy turned back containership SELEN departing from Sharjah to Karachi near the Hormuz approach, with IRGC Rear Admiral Tangsiri claiming all vessels must now coordinate passage with Iran's maritime authorities.
Only a trickle of vessels have crossed the waterway since the war began, many of them Iranian-linked. Iran's parliament is advancing a proposal to formalize the toll as a 'secure shipping route' fee.

A vessel using a false identity stolen from a scrapped ship has begun operating a shuttle service believed to transport Iranian oil through Hormuz, exploiting AIS tracking and a clean IMO number to bypass compliance checks.

stories.headline: Denmark's Social Democrats Win Election but Slump to Worst Result Since 1903, No Majority

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats won the most votes with 21.9% but suffered their worst result since 1903, down from 27.6% in the 2022 election.
The Liberals (Venstre) also had their worst showing in over a century with 10.1%, falling behind the Green Left SF which came second with 11.5% of the vote.
Neither the left-wing nor right-wing bloc secured the 90 seats needed for a majority, setting up coalition talks where centrist former PM Lars Løkke Rasmussen could be kingmaker.
The Danish People's Party (DF) and the Green Left SF were the biggest gainers, with DF rebounding to 9.2% of the vote.
The campaign focused on domestic issues rather than Frederiksen's handling of the Greenland crisis triggered by Trump's territorial ambitions.

stories.headline: Epic Games Lays Off 1,000+ Employees Citing Fortnite Engagement Downturn

key_facts.fact: Epic Games is laying off over 1,000 employees, approximately 20% of its workforce, with CEO Tim Sweeney citing 'the downturn in Fortnite engagement that started in 2025' leaving the company 'spending significantly more than we're making.'
The layoffs combined with $500 million in identified cost savings from contracting, marketing, and closing open roles are intended to stabilize the company financially.

Sweeney explicitly stated the layoffs 'aren't related to AI,' citing industry-wide challenges including slower growth, weaker consumer spending, and current consoles selling fewer units than the previous generation.
Epic recently raised V-Bucks prices, its Fortnite in-game currency, to 'help pay the bills' amid increased operating costs. This follows 830 layoffs in 2023.

stories.headline: Jamie Dimon Warns AI Could Displace Jobs Faster Than Internet, Calls for Govt-Business Response

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that AI could cost US jobs and suggested the government create an incentive system for businesses to retrain workers, fund early retirement, and relocate displaced employees.

Dimon warned that AI-driven economic changes may happen faster than other recent technological disruptions like the internet, speaking at the Hill and Valley Forum in Washington alongside Palantir defense chief Mike Gallagher.

Dimon said the response 'can't be just government' and must involve private sector collaboration, calling for a system where businesses are incentivized to do 'the right thing' in workforce transition.

stories.headline: First Parkinson's Patients Dosed in Phase 2 Trial of NLRP3 Inhibitor Dapansutrile

key_facts.fact: Olatec Therapeutics announced the first two patients have been randomized in DAPA-PD, a 12-month Phase 2 clinical trial of dapansutrile for Parkinson's disease at Cambridge University Hospitals.

The trial is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study led by Dr. Caroline Williams-Gray, measuring safety, tolerability, and changes in systemic and neuroinflammatory biomarkers including PET brain imaging.

Dapansutrile is also in Phase 2/3 for gout, Phase 2 for advanced melanoma (with Duke Cancer Institute and Merck), and Phase 2 for type 2 diabetes, making it one of the broadest NLRP3 inhibitor clinical programs.
The trial is funded by Cure Parkinson's and Van Andel Institute, targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway increasingly linked to neurodegeneration.
